questions.question: A task needs whole-input understanding with every token informing the verdict. Which architecture fits?
options: Left-to-right generation only
No model at all, pure rules
Random token sampling
Bidirectional encoding of the full input
questions.explanation: Understanding reads both directions. This lesson masks and predicts for encoder representations.

questions.question: For a selected ordinary token t, what does labels[i] store?
options: IGNORE_INDEX=-100 for every selected token
The replacement ID, always 0 for [MASK]
The token position i multiplied by vocab_size
The original token ID t, even if input_ids[i] is replaced by [MASK]
questions.explanation: Labels preserve the original target at selected positions; unselected positions alone retain IGNORE_INDEX.

questions.question: Under the 80/10/10 branch in create_mlm_batch, what happens when the second random draw r is 0.85?
options: The token is replaced by a different non-special random vocabulary ID
The token is replaced by MASK_ID=0
The input token is left unchanged and its label is ignored
The whole sentence is discarded
questions.explanation: The branch 0.8 <= r < 0.9 samples a random ID, excluding special IDs and the original token.

questions.question: What does whole_word_mlm do when a selected span covers two subword IDs?
options: It selects only the first subword and drops the second from the input
It assigns both original IDs as labels and applies the same masking choice to both positions
It creates one label for the span and changes neither input token
It skips the span because only single-token words can be masked
questions.explanation: A selected word span is handled as a unit: each position receives its original label and the chosen mask/random/unchanged operation.

questions.question: Why does an unselected position receive IGNORE_INDEX=-100 in this toy MLM batch?
options: It marks a [MASK] token that must be copied to the output
-100 is the vocabulary ID reserved for punctuation
The loss can exclude that position instead of asking the model to predict every input token
It forces the model to predict the [CLS] token twice
questions.explanation: The sentinel label distinguishes positions used for the MLM objective from positions that were merely observed.

questions.question: What distribution does toy_predict(masked_inputs, vocab) return for each input position?
options: A random vector whose entries do not sum to one
A one-hot vector for MASK_ID
A vector containing only the original unmasked token
A uniform vector with one probability 1/len(vocab) for every vocabulary item
questions.explanation: toy_predict builds `[1.0 / V for _ in vocab]` independently for every masked input.
